text_summary.body: Daniel continued until the first year of King Cyrus.

setting.body: Babylonian documents count Cyrus's years from the fall of Babylon with an accession year; year 1 began 1 Nisan = 24 Mar 538 (Parker & Dubberstein). Daniel 10:1 dates a later vision to Cyrus's third year, so 1:21 is commonly read as marking the end of the Babylonian era of his service rather than his death.

constraints.textual_assertion: Daniel continued even to the first year of King Cyrus
assumptions: Counted in Babylonian years (accession year 539/538 not counted): year 1 = 24 Mar 538 – 12 Mar 537. Counting the accession year as year 1 would move the window about five months earlier (Oct 539 – Mar 538).

open_questions: The reading of 1:21 alongside 10:1 is to be revisited with Daniel 10.

not_applicable.commentary: Enduring Word on Daniel 1 does not discuss 1:21 in detail (checked in session 1).
not_applicable.competing_reconstructions: No competing historical reconstructions were found in the sources consulted; the accession-year counting alternative is recorded in the constraint assumptions.
